video_title: Why AI Memory Prices Are Exploding: The Silent Silicon War

scenes.narration: Over the past two years, spot market prices for enterprise memory have surged by more than two hundred percent. What began as a routine tech cycle has morphed into a historic silicon bottleneck.
scenes.visual_description: Massive glowing statistic showing the enterprise DRAM and spot market price explosion across 2024 to 2026.
scenes.animation: Count up from +0% to +500% over 1.2s with neon cyan glow and pulsing backdrop.
scenes.narrative_purpose: Hook viewer with the sudden reality of skyrocketing memory prices

scenes.narration: To feed modern AI processors, manufacturers must use High Bandwidth Memory. But here is the catch: producing one gigabyte of HBM takes three times as much physical silicon wafer area as standard DDR5.
scenes.visual_description: Split architectural comparison contrasting conventional DDR5 wafer usage with 3D Through-Silicon Via (TSV) HBM stacks.
scenes.animation: Wafers slide into view with dimension callouts highlighting the 300% surface area deficit.
scenes.narrative_purpose: Explain the 3x silicon penalty of HBM vs standard DDR5

scenes.narration: By mid-2024, memory giants SK Hynix and Micron dropped an unprecedented bombshell: their entire production lines were sold out through 2025, with major customer allocations already locked in for 2026.
scenes.visual_description: Milestone timeline tracking SK Hynix and Micron announcements locking out spot customers through 2026.
scenes.animation: Chronological nodes ignite in sequence with critical sell-out milestone badges.
scenes.narrative_purpose: Demonstrate the market sell-out across SK Hynix and Micron

scenes.narration: Even with wafers pressed, chips cannot ship without advanced packaging. TSMC's CoWoS packaging lines are stretched to the limit, with order wait times exceeding fifty-two weeks.
scenes.visual_description: Technical cross-section diagram of TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging interposer bonding GPU logic and HBM3e stacks.
scenes.animation: Data streams pulse between silicon dies through the interposer with lead time warnings.
scenes.narrative_purpose: Highlight the CoWoS packaging choke point at TSMC

scenes.narration: Because memory fabs shifted eighty percent of new investment into AI silicon, standard memory inventories collapsed from sixteen weeks down to three. The AI boom is actively cannibalizing consumer tech.
scenes.visual_description: Plunging inventory curve tracking global channel buffers dropping from 16 weeks down to critical 3 weeks.
scenes.animation: Dynamic line graph plunges downwards with red warning accenting the supply deficit.
scenes.narrative_purpose: Explain the siphon effect on consumer PCs and smartphones
